scope: DECISIVE: both values take the SAME branch (0x471C41) and decode ONE delta, so the landing codec itself is variable-length
conclusion: the branch is IDENTICAL for both values, so explanation (a) from the previous round is ruled out
the landing codec is therefore VARIABLE-LENGTH: the same field costs 33 bits for 0x100 and 75 bits for 5830 (97 minus the 22 non-value bits)
that also explains why the codec description in cols (-97 = 1 bit gate + LE32) does not hold on this path - this build uses a variable form
the_relationship_to_measure: the only remaining unknown is the function value -> bit length
measuring it at 3-4 magnitudes (e.g. 0x100, 0x200, 0x1000, 5830) gives the table, and with that table any value can be encoded with a known length
each measurement is one session, so this is a bounded, finite task rather than an open-ended search
why_this_is_the_right_next_step: the framing is already pinned (55 bits for one field with a zero-ish value)
the codec is the only variable left, and it is a monotone function of the value in all likely encodings
